pages.title: About the Practice
pages.hint: The story of a new comprehensive family dental office in West Alexandria: founded by Dr. Sameer Atrash (Fairfax-raised, Tufts-trained) with Dr. Fadi Alhrashi; 'complete care, one dental home' philosophy; evening and weekend hours; four languages; insurance including Virginia Medicaid; comfort options; what 'no assembly-line dentistry' means in practice (time, explanation, written costs, no pressure). Sections: Why we opened here, How a visit works, What we treat, The office (Bradlee Office Building, free parking, off I-395), Who you will meet. Link to dentists, technology, our approach, areas.

pages.title: Our Approach
pages.hint: How the practice works, as plain commitments: we explain before we touch anything, we show you the image on the screen, costs in writing before treatment, honest about what needs doing now vs what can be watched, you decide without pressure, comfort planning for nervous patients (stop signal, pacing, nitrous oxide, sedation after review), one dental home for the whole family across every stage. Include a 'what we will not do' list (no surprise bills, no lectures, no selling the more expensive option when a simpler one is right).

pages.title: Technology
pages.hint: Technology used when it meaningfully improves care: 3D imaging (cone-beam CT) for implant planning, wisdom teeth and complex cases; magnification for precision; digital X-rays with far less exposure than film and images shown on the screen beside you; digital records with secure online registration (Denticon) before your visit; online booking. Frame each as 'what it does for you'. Do NOT claim intraoral scanners, lasers, same-day crowns or any other specific equipment. End with 'technology is the tool, the relationship is the point'.

pages.title: New Patients
pages.hint: Landing page for new patients: welcome, how to book (online 24/7 or call), what to bring, hours that fit real schedules (7 AM–8 PM weekdays, weekend mornings), insurance including Virginia Medicaid, four languages, comfort options, paperwork online before you arrive, what the first visit looks like. Friendly and practical.

pages.title: Your First Visit
pages.hint: Step by step: booking, forms online via Denticon before you arrive, what to bring (ID, insurance card, medication list, recent X-rays), the conversation first, the exam (gums measured, every tooth, bite, oral cancer screening), X-rays only when needed, whether a cleaning happens the same day (healthy gums yes; gum disease needs a deeper cleaning planned separately), a written plan with costs and no pressure, how long to allow (about 60–90 minutes), evening and weekend availability for the first visit.

pages.title: Understanding Dental Insurance
pages.hint: Plain-English explainer: premium, deductible, annual maximum, coinsurance/copay, in-network vs out-of-network, the typical 100/80/50 structure (preventive, basic, major) and that plans vary, waiting periods, frequency limits (two cleanings a year, X-ray intervals), pre-treatment estimates, why 'covered' is not the same as 'free', end-of-year benefits. pages.title: Virginia Medicaid Dental
pages.hint: This office accepts Virginia Medicaid, which is uncommon in Northern Virginia for a comprehensive family practice. Explain in general terms that Virginia's Medicaid program includes dental benefits for children and, since 2021, for adults (Cardinal Care / Smiles For Children is the dental program administered by DentaQuest); say benefits and covered services vary by eligibility category and that the office will check your coverage before your visit. Keep claims general and hedged ('coverage details change; we will confirm what your plan covers'). What to bring (Medicaid ID), same care and same hours as every patient, no separate waiting room or schedule. Link to insurance and first visit.

pages.title: No Insurance? No Problem
pages.hint: Paying without insurance: written estimate before anything starts, priorities explained so you can stage treatment, prevention is the cheapest dentistry, ask about payment options when you call (do NOT name any financing company or invent a membership plan or prices), a problem-focused exam is a sensible first step if something hurts, and Virginia Medicaid may be an option for those who qualify. Honest and reassuring.
